content: Build or revise a real Python project. Return JSON {"files": {"module.py": "complete source", ...}}. Use Python stdlib. Put substantive helpers in a separate module and import them from the entrypoint module. Write complete replacements for changed files; unchanged parent files are preserved automatically. The entrypoint receives the input value itself, never the test-case wrapper. Preserve existing behavior while adding the requirement. Match the exact expected output type and keys. Do not hardcode example data. All execution and file writes happen in an isolated temporary project inside Docker. No network or subprocess.

{"development_example":{"expected":{"order":[]},"input":{"data":[],"options":{}}},"entrypoint":"scheduler:solve","failure_feedback":"ValueError: Expected only files mapping","parent_files":{},"requirement":"Build scheduler.py with solve(value), plus a helper module. value is {data: tasks, options: {}}. Each task has id (string), status, priority (integer, default 0), dependencies (list of ids, default []). Return {order: [ids]} containing only queued or retry tasks whose every dependency exists and has status tested. A queued dependency is not complete, even if it appears earlier in the output. Missing or failed dependencies block the task. Sort eligible tasks by descending priority, then ascending id. Never include running, tested, failed or cancelled tasks. Do not mutate input."}
